name: EPA SOBE (eRule Phase 2) sewer overflow and bypass event reports, Mississippi permits
operator: US EPA (filed by permittees through NeT-SewerOverflow to MDEQ)
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water named in a child table (e.g. "Davis bayou", "Mississippi River")
access_detail: ECHO daily ZIP current_sewer_overflow_and_collection_systems_tables.zip; tables sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv (+ receiving_waters, causes, impacts, types, corrective_actions). 353 Mississippi events from 47 permits on 2026-11-03 (latest start 2026-10-28); a few from 2023-2024, the rest from January 2026 on (125 in June 2026). Median 4 days from start to EPA receipt. Sample raw/sobe-ms-sample.json.
cadence: Daily ZIP; the 5-day written report is due within 5 days of awareness, so events appear about 4 days (median) after they start.
history: Sparse before December 2025 (eRule effective 2025-12-21); full from January 2026.
license: EPA ECHO data: public domain (US government work).
status_reason: Read by the national eRule ingester with Mississippi in its states (Central time, free text scrubbed): the all-versions extract of 2026-11-04 held 358 current Mississippi events from 47 permits (SSO 314, bypass 43, CSO 1); 248 kept from 27 permits (243 naming a receiving water), 110 dropped (108 naming no water with only land or no observable impacts, 1 building backup, 1 bypass whose water is 'None'). Report received a median 4 days after the start (90th percentile 41 days). Every row has coordinates; 15 have no volume.
notes: The current-version ZIP held only its metadata file on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-07; the module reads the current version of each report from the all-versions ZIP. The City of Jackson's reports give creek names without 'Creek' ('EUBANKS', 'TOWN'); eight are read as the NHD creek of that name near the reports' points, four (Belhaven, Caney, Eastover, Three Mile) are kept as typed.

name: MDEQ "Reporting Sanitary Sewer Overflows or Bypasses in Mississippi" (NeT-SewerOverflow flyer)
status_reason: Regulator-report deadlines (24 hours; 5-day electronic report from 2025-12-21).

name: Mississippi Beach Monitoring Program (BeachMonitoringView FeatureServer)
operator: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality with USM Gulf Coast Research Laboratory
waters_covered: 21 Gulf Coast beach stations (Hancock, Harrison, Jackson counties) and their beach segments
access_detail: Layer 0 stations (points), layer 1 beach segments (lines), both public: https://mgis19.mdeq.ms.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Hosted/BeachMonitoringView/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json. Fields isadvisory, isclosure, eventtype (Enterococci, Debris Clean Up, HAB), advisorydesc, closuredesc, startdate, lastsampledate, epa (BEACON id). 21 stations, none under advisory on 2026-11-03. Map at beaches.mdeq.ms.gov (historical results and advisories pages /Historical/HBR, /Historical/HCA). Samples raw/beach-l0.json, raw/beach-l1.json.
cannot_fill: ended_at (advisory lift is a state change only)
cadence: Weekly sampling in season (Gulf Coast Research Laboratory); advisories posted first on the map. From 2026-09-08 routine advisories go to beach signs and the website only (no texts or press releases), per local press.
history: Historical pages on the site; layer holds current state
status_reason: Best beach feed in the group, not yet read: an advisory and a closure are two separate flags on each station, with MDEQ's own start date as text and no end. The generic snapshot reader takes one state field and dates events by poll, which would drop MDEQ's start date and the closure flag; the generic layer reader would keep a lifted advisory in effect until it ages out. No station was under advisory or closure on 2026-11-07 (21 stations, Enterococci, last samples 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-05), so the lifted state could not be observed. Needs a small module (both flags, the start date, lifted when the flags clear).

name: MDEQ beach advisory text and email alerts
access_detail: Older posts: text "MDEQbeach" to 95577; email list on request; X @MDEQ; news releases per advisory change. 2026 press says texts and releases ran through 2026-09-07 only.
status_reason: Retired for routine advisories on 2026-09-08 (MDEQ news release of that day: "communicated through posted beach signage and the MDEQ Beach Monitoring website rather than text alerts and news releases"); the beach layer is the source.

name: JXN Water (Jackson sewer under federal interim stipulated order, 2023)
operator: JXN Water (federal court-appointed interim third-party manager for the City of Jackson sewer system)
waters_covered: Pearl River, Town Creek, Lynch Creek, Hanging Moss Creek, Eubanks Creek (Jackson)
access_detail: Quarterly status reports to the court and public under the 2023 order; Jackson's Sewer Overflow Response Plan calls for a news release and temporary signs for significant overflows (per press). No public overflow dashboard found. Jackson permits MS0024295 (Savanna Street, 78 SOBE events) and MS0044059 (Trahon/Big Creek, 11) also file in SOBE.
legal_basis: EPA/MDEQ consent decree (2013) and 2023 interim stipulated order
status_reason: Events reach SOBE; quarterly reports give totals.

name: MDEQ water contact advisories for rivers after large SSOs (e.g. Pearl River)
waters_covered: Pearl River and others ad hoc
access_detail: MDEQ's news-release RSS feed (answered 200 on 2026-11-07). The 2026-09-02 release issued a water contact advisory for an unnamed tributary of Trahon Creek and Trahon Creek to the Pearl River "due to an ongoing sewage bypass" and said "the longstanding water contact advisory for the section of the Pearl River from Hanging Moss Creek to the Byram Swinging bridge remains in effect". No standing list of advisories in effect.
cadence: ad hoc; releases a few times a month
status_reason: Polled every 3 hours by the notice-register monitor (row ms-mdeq-news-releases): a new release naming a water contact advisory becomes a dated record. The advisories in effect before the first poll (the Pearl River below Jackson, Trahon Creek) are not records.

name: MDEQ Current_NPDES_Points hosted layer
access_detail: FeatureServer/0 public; fields are the facility's addresses, basin, county and agency staff assignments; no outfall number or receiving water.
status_reason: Facility points of every MDEQ-regulated site (9,188 rows on 2026-11-07: plant entrances, addresses and agency staff assignments), not outfall points; no improvement on EPA's permitted-feature points.

name: Mississippi HABs
waters_covered: Gulf beaches (HAB event type in the beach layer); freshwater: MDEQ news releases
access_detail: The beach layer carries eventtype HAB for advisories and closures. MDEQ has issued freshwater HAB advisories by news release (e.g. Ross Barnett Reservoir) per press; no freshwater list found.
status_reason: Coastal HAB advisories and closures as eventtype HAB on the beach layer; read with it when that module is built.
